questions.prompt: Which is the best definition of matter?
options: Anything that is made in a factory
Anything that has mass and takes up space

feedback.1: Air is matter, but you can't see it!
feedback.2: Liquids and gases are matter too.

questions.hint: Think of the two things every piece of matter has.
questions.explain: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space (volume). Being visible or solid does not matter.

questions.prompt: Sort these into matter and not matter.
questions.hint: Ask: does it have mass? Does it take up space?
questions.explain: Water, air, dust and steam all have mass and volume. Light, sound and heat are forms of energy, and anger is a feeling: none of them are matter.

questions.prompt: You smell a perfume from across the room. What reaches your nose?
options: Nothing, smell is just an idea
questions.hint: Smell must be carried by something real.
questions.explain: Tiny particles of perfume travel through the air and reach your nose. Those particles are matter.

questions.text: Matter is anything that has ___ and occupies ___.
questions.explain: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.

questions.prompt: Which of these are forms of ENERGY rather than matter? Choose all that apply.
questions.hint: Oxygen and raindrops can be weighed. Can the others?
questions.explain: Light (including rainbow colours), sound and heat are energy. Oxygen gas and raindrops are matter.

questions.prompt: Two balloons balance on a ruler. One is popped and the side with the full balloon goes down. What is the INDEPENDENT variable?
questions.hint: The independent variable is the one YOU change on purpose.
questions.explain: You changed whether a balloon contained air (independent variable) and observed which way the ruler tipped (dependent variable).

questions.prompt: A glass with a dry tissue at the bottom is pushed upside-down into water. The tissue stays dry. This shows that air…
questions.explain: Air trapped in the glass takes up space, so water can't enter and wet the tissue.

questions.prompt: 1 m³ of air has a mass of about 1.2 kg. A room is 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. Roughly what is the mass of air in the room, in kg?
questions.hint: First find the volume: length × width × height. Then multiply by 1.2.
questions.explain: Volume = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 m³. Mass = 60 × 1.2 = 72 kg. Air is surprisingly heavy!

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.right: Amount of stuff in an object
Amount of space something takes up
Light, heat and sound are forms of this

questions.explain: Mass = amount of stuff; volume = space taken up; matter has both; light, heat and sound are energy.

questions.prompt: Your friend says, 'A shadow must be matter because I can see it.' Explain why your friend is wrong.
questions.modelAnswer: Seeing something does not make it matter. A shadow is just an area where light is blocked by an object. It has no mass and takes up no space, so it is not matter.
rubric: I said a shadow has no mass
I said a shadow does not take up space
I explained that a shadow is where light is blocked
questions.explain: Always test with the two rules: mass and volume. A shadow has neither.
